To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Amplex Red reagent is a convenient tool for the detection of the mitochondrial ROS generation by intact mitochondria or submitochondrial particles, and (2) the initial rates of ROS generation by intact or submitochondrial particle preparations, not the total amount of resorufen accumulated during the incubation, should be taken for the assessment of mitochondrial ROS-generating activities.

(1) mitochondrial ROS-generating systems, i.e. respiratory complexes and RET, are linearly dependent on oxygen concentration within a range of ~125-750 μM; (2) the mitochondrial ROS-generators are not affected by their prolonged operation; and (3) the initial rates, not the amount, of ROS production should be taken as a measure of the mitochondrial activity.
the initial rate of resorufins formation in the Amlex Red assay is a reliable measure of the rate of mitochondrial ROS production and that it follows the first order oxygen dependence.
